topics.label: Introduction and overview of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's objectives, historical framework, and the conceptual model of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and signaling pathway deregulation
topics.groupedBecause: They detail the oncogenic mutations and signaling cascades that confer growth signal autonomy and allow cells to bypass growth inhibition.

topics.label: Block to terminal differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer cells arrest normal maturation processes across hematopoietic and intestinal epithelial tissues.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis
topics.groupedBecause: It details how oncogenic alterations in p53 and Bcl-2 family proteins allow cancer cells to resist programmed cell death.

topics.label: Replicative immortality and cellular senescence bypass
topics.groupedBecause: They address the mechanisms of telomere maintenance, senescence bypass, and cellular stress responses that enable replicative immortality, concluding the discussion of cell-autonomous growth hallmarks.

topics.label: Cancer metabolic reprogramming
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer cells reprogram cellular metabolism to support growth through aerobic glycolysis and oncometabolite-driven epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the requirement and mechanisms for inducing new blood vessel formation to sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the biological barriers, circulation dynamics, microenvironmental interactions, and genomic profiles governing tumor metastasis.

topics.label: Lecture summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a summary of how hallmarks integrate across cancer development and final administrative remarks.
